name: Status Indicators
description: At-a-glance status for sessions: open questions, blocked, done, and free-form stages such as "waiting for CI", shown as badges.
guide: Keep the user's session status current so they can see at a glance who needs them. End EVERY final message with one line: [status: questions=N blocked=yes|no done=yes|no]. questions = open questions or decisions still waiting on the user, including earlier ones not yet answered; blocked = you cannot continue until they answer; done = ALL work assigned to you is finished or handed off (a todo written, returned to whoever assigned it), not merely this turn. Restate it every turn; a missing line leaves the old status in place. If you coordinate other sessions, mark them with `clideck status/stage "<label>" --you|--waiting|--active <session> ...` and reuse labels from `clideck status/stages`.

commands.name: report
commands.description: Set your status directly (omitted flags reset); the usual way is the end-of-turn line [status: questions=N blocked=yes|no done=yes|no]. questions = open questions for the user; blocked = you cannot continue until they answer; done = ALL assigned work finished or handed off.

commands.name: questions
commands.description: Record your open questions for the user, one short line each, so they can list them later. Replaces your earlier list; no arguments lists it. Only needed when the list changes.

commands.name: stage
commands.description: Mark a session's stage with a free-form label and who must act: --you (the user), --waiting (something outside, such as CI or review) or --active (work in progress). Names none or several sessions (default: yourself); --clear removes it. Reuse labels from status/stages. --icon adds an optional emoji.

commands.name: stages
commands.description: List the stage labels already in use in your project, with their levels and counts, so you reuse them instead of inventing variants.

commands.name: list
commands.description: Show each session's status (stage, open questions, blocked, done) in your project.
